guidelineVersions: BOAST: The management of children with acute musculoskeletal infection (May 2022)

brief.scenario: Owen Castleford, 16, has had two weeks of worsening right shoulder pain after a feverish illness. He is holding the arm still. Temperature 38.2°C, heart rate 96, blood pressure normal.
brief.task: The examiner will give you his blood results and an MRI report, and later read out the findings of a radiograph. Interpret them, explain the pathology and outline management.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Metaphysis, pus, pressure, periosteum. Culture before antibiotics if he is stable.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Starting oral antibiotics and sending him home, or ignoring the subperiosteal collection.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This is acute haematogenous osteomyelitis of the proximal humeral metaphysis with a subperiosteal abscess."

grid.label: Interprets the MRI
grid.fail: Reads it as a fracture or reassures without considering infection.
grid.pass: Acute haematogenous osteomyelitis of the proximal humeral metaphysis with a subperiosteal abscess.
grid.high: Keeps Ewing sarcoma in the differential for periosteal reaction, so sends tissue for histology as well as culture.

grid.label: Pathogenesis
grid.fail: Cannot explain why the metaphysis is involved.
grid.pass: Bacteraemia seeds the metaphysis, where looping vessels slow flow; pus raises pressure, lifts the periosteum and kills cortex.
grid.high: Proximal humeral metaphysis is intracapsular, so pus can enter the shoulder joint; Staphylococcus aureus is the usual organism.

grid.label: Investigations
grid.fail: Relies on a normal radiograph to exclude infection.
grid.pass: FBC, CRP, blood cultures, ESR and plain radiographs; radiographs are often normal early, MRI is the second-line test.
grid.high: Blood culture at least 2 ml; MRI ideally within 48 hours; ultrasound for joint effusion in the same time frame.

grid.label: Management
grid.fail: Gives oral antibiotics and discharges, or delays antibiotics in a septic patient to wait for theatre.
grid.pass: Blood cultures, IV antibiotics; drain the abscess with deep samples. If stable and surgery planned, antibiotics may wait for sampling.
grid.high: Oral switch and duration guided by temperature, CRP, ESR and white count; PICC if IV continues; follow-up at least 12 months.

grid.label: Chronic osteomyelitis from the radiograph findings
grid.fail: Confuses sequestrum with involucrum, or says antibiotics alone cure chronic disease.
grid.pass: Sequestrum: dead bone. Involucrum: new periosteal bone around it. Chronic disease needs debridement plus antibiotics.
grid.high: Explains antibiotics cannot reach avascular sequestrum; names cloaca and sinus, and squamous carcinoma (Marjolin's ulcer) in a long-standing sinus.

grid.label: Cierny-Mader staging
grid.fail: Mixes up anatomical types and host classes.
grid.pass: Anatomical types 1 medullary, 2 superficial, 3 localised, 4 diffuse. Host A normal, B compromised, C treatment worse than the disease.
grid.high: Splits B into local and systemic compromise, and says stage guides debridement, reconstruction or suppression.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: MRI shows metaphyseal oedema and a subperiosteal collection. What is it?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Probably a stress fracture from sport.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'm not sure, it's just where it happens.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: His X-ray is normal. Does that help?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, a normal X-ray makes osteomyelitis unlikely.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Oral flucloxacillin and review in clinic.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Here are the radiograph findings from another patient. What is the dense fragment?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That's the involucrum. Antibiotics should clear it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Type A is acute and type C is chronic.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: WCC 14.8, CRP 86, ESR 60. MRI shows metaphyseal oedema, periosteal elevation and a subperiosteal collection.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Acute haematogenous osteomyelitis of the proximal humeral metaphysis with a subperiosteal abscess.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Bacteraemia seeds the metaphysis, where looping vessels slow blood flow. Pus raises pressure, lifts the periosteum and the cortex dies.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: FBC, CRP, blood cultures and ESR, and plain radiographs. X-rays are often normal early, so MRI is the next test.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Blood cultures, then IV antibiotics. The abscess needs drainage with deep samples. He's stable, so antibiotics can wait for theatre sampling if it's soon.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Here are the radiograph findings from another patient.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A sequestrum, which is dead bone, inside an involucrum of new periosteal bone. Chronic osteomyelitis needs debridement plus antibiotics.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How would you classify chronic osteomyelitis?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Cierny-Mader: types 1 medullary, 2 superficial, 3 localised, 4 diffuse. Hosts A normal, B compromised, C treatment worse than the disease.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Ewing sarcoma can mimic this with periosteal reaction, so I'd send tissue for histology as well as culture.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The MRI also shows a small shoulder effusion.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The proximal humeral metaphysis is intracapsular, so pus can enter the joint. I'd want the joint assessed for septic arthritis. Staph aureus is the usual organism.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Blood culture at least 2 ml, MRI ideally within 48 hours, and ultrasound of the joint in the same window.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: When would you switch to oral?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: When temperature, CRP, ESR and white count are improving with the clinical picture. A PICC if IV has to continue, and follow-up for at least 12 months.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why doesn't chronic infection clear with antibiotics?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The sequestrum is avascular, so antibiotics can't reach it. Pus escapes through a cloaca to a sinus, and a long-standing sinus can develop squamous carcinoma, Marjolin's ulcer.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Host B splits into local and systemic compromise, and the stage guides whether we debride and reconstruct or aim for suppression.

failures.move: Oral antibiotics and discharge with a subperiosteal abscess.
failures.consequence: Undrained pus spreads, with risk of septic arthritis, growth disturbance and chronic infection.

failures.move: Accepting a normal early radiograph as excluding infection.
failures.consequence: Delayed diagnosis while bone necrosis progresses.

failures.move: Culturing but not sending tissue for histology.
failures.consequence: A Ewing sarcoma mimicking infection could be missed.

failures.move: Treating chronic osteomyelitis with antibiotics alone.
failures.consequence: Dead bone remains and infection recurs.

recovery.line: Metaphysis, pus, pressure, periosteum, dead bone.
Immediately if he is septic; if stable and theatre is imminent, after deep samples.

knowledge.fact: Metaphyseal vessels loop and slow, so bacteria settle there in growing bone.
BOAST: FBC, CRP, blood cultures, ESR; radiographs; MRI second line.
Antibiotics immediately if high-risk sepsis; if stable and surgery planned, may delay for deep samples.
Chronic osteomyelitis: sequestrum needs debridement as well as antibiotics.
Cierny-Mader: anatomical types 1 to 4; hosts A, B, C.

recall.think: Sepsis, septic arthritis, and a tumour mimicking infection.
recall.say: "Acute haematogenous osteomyelitis with a subperiosteal abscess."
do: IV antibiotics; drain abscess with deep samples
recall.finish: Drainage, IV then oral antibiotics guided by response, long follow-up.

sources.name: British Orthopaedic Association Standard for Trauma (BOAST): The management of children with acute musculoskeletal infection
sources.supports: Investigations (FBC, CRP, blood cultures of at least 2 ml, ESR, radiographs), MRI within 48 hours, ultrasound, immediate antibiotics in high-risk sepsis, delaying antibiotics for deep sampling when stable, surgery for abscess, IV-to-oral switch guided by markers, PICC, 12-month follow-up

sources.supports: Haematogenous pathogenesis in the metaphysis; Staphylococcus aureus as the main organism; IV then oral treatment

sources.supports: Bone sampling for microbiology and pathology; sequestrum in chronic osteomyelitis; surgical debridement needed for cure

sources.supports: Acute and chronic osteomyelitis: intracapsular metaphyses, sequestrum, involucrum, cloaca, Marjolin's ulcer; Ewing sarcoma as a differential

partner.opening: Here are Owen's blood results and his MRI. Tell me what is going on.

reveals.finding: WCC 14.8 ×10⁹/L, CRP 86 mg/L, ESR 60 mm/h. Blood cultures not yet taken.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for the MRI report
reveals.finding: Read out: coronal fat-suppressed MRI of the right humerus shows proximal humeral metaphyseal marrow oedema, periosteal elevation, a 15 mm subperiosteal collection and a small glenohumeral effusion. The growth plate is open.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for a radiograph of his shoulder

reveals.finding: This is a different patient, years after an open tibial fracture. Read out: the plain radiograph of the tibia shows a thickened, irregular shaft. Within the medullary cavity lies a dense, sharply outlined fragment of bone about 3 cm long, separated from the bone around it by a thin lucent rim. Surrounding it is a thick, irregular shell of new bone formed beneath the lifted periosteum. A small rounded defect passes through this shell towards the skin.

push.question: Why does this start in the metaphysis?
push.expect: Looping vessels, slow flow, bacteria settle.

push.question: When would you give the first antibiotic dose?
push.expect: After blood cultures; immediately if septic; after deep samples if stable and theatre is imminent.

push.question: What does the collection change?
push.expect: Surgical drainage with samples for culture and histology.

push.question: Name the features described on this radiograph.

curveballs.prompt: He becomes hypotensive and his lactate is 4.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Treat as sepsis: blood cultures and IV antibiotics immediately, resuscitate, escalate; do not wait for theatre.

curveballs.prompt: Culture is negative but the histology shows small round blue cells.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Possible Ewing sarcoma: refer to a bone sarcoma centre.
Subacute osteomyelitis: a localised abscess walled off by sclerotic bone.
